Both disclosures describe the key activities of the CRM Framework for managing compliance risk, specifically listing legal compliance monitoring, employee training, risk appetite monitoring, compliance assessments, and issue remediation. The 2025 text is nearly identical to the 2024 text.

The 2024 disclosure describes the establishment of the CRM Policy for standardization and oversight by ICRM. The 2025 disclosure (c_2025_7_D375) includes a sentence explicitly stating the purpose of the CRM Policy is to 'achieve standardization and centralization' and mentions Citi's obligation to mitigate compliance risks. While the specific mention of ICRM oversight in the 2025 D375 sentence is less prominent than in 2024 D426, the subject matter (CRM Policy standardization) is present. However, looking at the automatic search, c_2025_7_D374 discusses ICRM's primary objectives and oversight of the CRM Framework. c_2025_7_D375 focuses on the framework activities. The 2024 D426 text 'To anticipate, control and mitigate compliance risk, Citi has established the CRM Policy to achieve standardization...' is literally present in c_2025_7_D375 (Sentence 7). Therefore, c_2025_7_D375 is a match. Note: T

comparisons.peer_topic: Scope of Compliance Risk Management Program
comparisons.peer_summary: The Compliance Risk Management Program, administered by Compliance, assesses and monitors compliance and reputational risks, designs and implements controls and training, conducts independent testing, investigates breaches, and leads responses to regulatory examinations and inquiries.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and Goldman Sachs (GS) disclose specific operational components of their compliance risk management frameworks beyond just definitions. Citi’s CRM Framework includes activities such as 'identifying and analyzing changes' in laws and 'executing Compliance Risk Assessments' to ensure conformance. Similarly, GS’s Compliance Risk Management Program involves assessing risks, 'monitoring for compliance with new or amended laws, rules and regulations,' and conducting 'independent testing.' While Citi emphasizes 'issue identification, escalation and remediation' to drive accountability, GS highlights 'investigates, surveils and monitors for compliance risks and breaches' and leading responses to regulatory examinations, showing a shared focus on proactive monitoring, assessment, and responsive action to regulatory changes.

sentences.text: • Management of Citi's compliance with laws, rules and regulations by identifying and analyzing changes, assessing the impact and implementing appropriate policies, processes and controls;

• Executing Compliance Risk Assessments, the results of which inform Compliance Risk Monitoring and testing of compliance risks and controls in assessing conformance with laws, rules, regulations and internal policies; and

• Issue identification, escalation and remediation to drive accountability, including measurement and reporting of compliance risk metrics against established thresholds in support of the CRM Policy and Compliance Risk Appetite.

Our Compliance Risk Management Program, administered by Compliance, assesses our compliance, regulatory and reputational risk; monitors for compliance with new or amended laws, rules and regulations; designs and implements controls, policies, procedures and training; conducts independent testing; investigates, surveils and monitors for compliance risks and breaches; and leads our responses to regulatory examinations, audits and inquiries.

comparisons.peer_topic: Compliance risk governance structure and ownership
comparisons.peer_summary: Line of Business (LOB) units and Corporate hold primary ownership and accountability for managing compliance risk, while the independent Operational Risk and Compliance organization provides independent review, monitoring, and oversight.
comparisons.comparison: Citi and JPMorgan both address the governance and ownership structure of compliance risk, though with different emphases. Citi’s disclosure outlines a framework where responsibilities are fulfilled through integrated key activities, implicitly supporting a structure of accountability through 'issue identification, escalation and remediation.' JPMorgan explicitly defines the ownership structure, stating that Line of Business (LOB) units and Corporate hold 'primary ownership of and accountability for managing their compliance risk,' while an independent organization provides 'independent review, monitoring and oversight.' Both companies rely on a combination of business-unit accountability and independent oversight functions to manage compliance risk, aligning with the three-lines-of-defense model implied in Citi’s framework activities.

sentences.text: • Issue identification, escalation and remediation to drive accountability, including measurement and reporting of compliance risk metrics against established thresholds in support of the CRM Policy and Compliance Risk Appetite.
Each of the LOBs and Corporate hold primary ownership of and accountability for managing their compliance risk.

The Firm's Operational Risk and Compliance Organization ("Operational Risk and Compliance"), which is independent of the LOBs and Corporate, provides independent review, monitoring and oversight of business operations with a focus on compliance with the laws, rules, and regulations applicable to the delivery of the Firm's products and services to clients and customers.
